page: Microsoft Azure GS4-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, providing a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It is equipped with 224.0 GB of system memory, translating to an exceptionally high memory allocation of 56.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 459 GB, and there are no GPUs present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates that the compute performance of the GS4-4 is relatively modest. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng place the instance in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed; while the PassMark memory score achieves an average rating in the middle 50%, the large-block memory write bandwidth is categorized in the bottom 10%, and read bandwidth remains in the bottom 25%. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput also fall within the bottom 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the GS4-4 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. However, the older Intel Xeon E5 v3 architecture presents a tradeoff, as compute-heavy tasks will experience lower performance compared to newer generations. This instance is best suited for workloads such as in-memory caching, legacy database hosting, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that require a large RAM footprint but have low parallel processing demands.
